subject.title: Next Sprint B: model-input validation guardrails

question: Should configured model input keep audio/video as valid metadata with semantic guardrails, or should OpenClaw reject those modalities from chat-model config by default?
rationale: Current main deliberately accepts audio/video in config while other runtime paths still narrow or trust capability declarations, so automation cannot choose the permanent API contract without breaking one side of existing behavior.

options.title: Accept metadata plus guardrails
options.body: Keep audio/video as valid metadata, add trusted catalog/provider cross-checks, and surface clear diagnostics when a selected runtime cannot use a declared modality.

options.title: Reject unsupported inputs by default
options.body: Tighten configured model validation to fail unsupported modalities and include migration or override handling for existing multimodal configs.

options.title: Defer contract change
options.body: Leave current behavior in place until generated-catalog widening and media-output policy are settled together.

recommendation.title: Accept metadata plus guardrails
recommendation.body: Keep audio/video as valid metadata, add trusted catalog/provider cross-checks, and surface clear diagnostics when a selected runtime cannot use a declared modality.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest adjacent history across provider catalog, media defaults, and configured image resolver behavior for deciding the API/product contract.
